title: Fractional Long-Range Dependence Multi-Mode for Remaining Useful Life Prognosis of IGBT Under DC Voltage Control
abstract: Since the degradation process of IGBTs is a slowly varying nonstationary stochastic process with random switching among three modes (active region, saturation region, and cut-off region), remaining useful life (RUL) prediction of IGBTs remains an urgent research issue. This paper investigates IGBT RUL prediction under DC voltage-controlled operating conditions. First, a health feature parameter (HFP) is constructed via the weighted linear combination of gate voltage, collector voltage, and temperature for fault feature extraction of degradation processes. Second, the Markov state transition matrix describing the three operating modes of IGBTs is established. Furthermore, a long-range dependent fractional Weibull process (fWp) prognostic model with three-mode characteristics is developed. Finally, validation is carried out on the public NASA IGBT thermal overload aging dataset. Error analysis demonstrates that the proposed method achieves superior prediction accuracy compared with four prognostic approaches: APE, OSGP, TDNN-GP, and SA-NN.
title_zh: Fractional Long-Range Dependence Multi-Mode for Remaining Useful Life Prognosis of IGBT Under DC Voltage Control

title: Disturbance-responsive online lithium-ion battery SOH estimation and analytical knee-point tracking with a Dual-Weibull Physics-Inspired Model
abstract: Accurate online estimation of lithium-ion battery state of health (SOH) and knee points remains challenging because feature-based estimators can be sensitive to changes in input-data quality, whereas conventional empirical models may lack the flexibility. Therefore, this study proposes an online SOH and knee-point estimation framework comprising a Transformer-adaptive Kalman filter (AKF) branch, a Dual-Weibull Physics-Inspired Model (DWPIM), and a disturbance-responsive multi-feature Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) gate. The residual-based AKF is adopted to recursively smooth the Transformer output and provide a posterior covariance state. Inspired by Weibull function in reliability engineering, DWPIM is introduced for capturing degradation trajectory and tracking the knee point online. Finally, the MLP gate dynamically fuses the Transformer-AKF and DWPIM estimates using the two current branch outputs, the AKF posterior covariance state, and the difference between the branches. Experimental evaluation was conducted on the CALCE battery dataset to assess the trajectory-representation capability, disturbance robustness, and online knee-point estimation performance of the proposed framework. The DWPIM achieved R 2 = 0.9911 on the source-cell trajectory. Under original data and simulated data disturbance, the observation-assisted framework achieved SOH RMSE values of 0.0125–0.0217. For CS2_36, CS2_37, and CS2_38, the final-100 pointwise knee-estimation MAEs were 84.39, 22.94, and 17.42 cycles, respectively; CS2_37 and CS2_38 achieved persistent ±10% accuracy lead times of 162 and 213 cycles. Extended strict closed-loop evaluation on six additional cells produced SOH RMSE values of 0.0214–0.0499.
title_zh: Disturbance-responsive online lithium-ion battery SOH estimation and analytical knee-point tracking with a Dual-Weibull Physics-Inspired Model
